scope.spatial: Australia; occurrences inside terrestrial protected areas and within 10 km buffers (assigned to nearest PA).

focal_taxa.rationale: Nocturnal insectivores with evidence of ALAN sensitivity; aligns with Layer A hypothesis.
focal_taxa.expected_response: Negative association with ALAN or weaker positive association than controls.

negative_controls.group: Diurnal birds (Aves; Passeriformes; provider-matched to focal data where possible)
negative_controls.rationale: High observer effort; expected to be neutral or positively associated with ALAN due to sampling bias. Primary control will be provider-matched to dominant focal-data providers.
negative_controls.expected_response: Neutral/positive; if similar to focal taxa after provider-matching, interpret as bias.

negative_controls.rationale: Field-observation driven; provides non-nocturnal control. Deferred due to ALA download failures (DEC-026).
negative_controls.expected_response: Neutral/positive; strong negative would question ALAN-specific inference.

filters: Deduplicate per species per day per 1 km grid cell
bias_strategy.background: Target-group background sampled from all ALA records of the same class within the same time window and spatial scope.
sampling_covariates: Local record density (kernel of all ALA records)
sensitivity_checks: Vary buffer radius (inside, 1 km, 5 km, 10 km)
Exclude records within 5 km of major urban cores
falsification_checks: Run identical models on negative controls

go_no_go_criteria: >= 5,000 focal records after filtering within spatial scope
>= 80% of focal records have valid ALAN covariates
>= 5,000 records for the primary negative control group after filtering
Provider-matched control subset is feasible (dominant providers overlap between focal/control)
Bias controls (target-group background, spatial blocking) are feasible at national or stated regional scale
data_sources: Atlas of Living Australia (ALA) occurrence downloads (mixed provider licences; see ledger)
notes: Proceed to WP0.15 only if criteria are met; otherwise stop at descriptive summaries without causal language.
Layer B is optional and contingent on negative-control results.
If provider dominance is extreme, treat analysis as provider-/region-bounded case study.
Primary inference uses provider-matched dr368 subset; full multi-provider run is sensitivity only.
